partnershipPlan: A patient partner, an emergency physician and a primary care representative comment on the review question and on the committee summary before it is sent.
socialListening: No social media listening; the hospital's patient relations log is read for complaints about findings that were not followed up.

items.theme: Hearing about a finding by letter
items.quote: Composite paraphrase: The letter said there was a spot on my kidney and to see my doctor; I did not sleep until the appointment.
items.implication: Record worry as a balancing measure and look for studies of how findings were communicated.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I went to the emergency department for a fall, and two years later I learned the scan had shown something they wanted to check.
items.implication: Extract results for emergency-only patients from every report.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I order the scan for the fracture, the patient goes home, and the line about the adrenal lesion lands in an inbox nobody reads.
items.implication: Treat the responsible clinician as the key failure point in the review.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: One navigator can close most loops for lung nodules, but not for every finding in a department this size.
items.implication: Extract resources per approach alongside completion.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: If every incidental finding comes to us, we need to know it is expected and what the interval is.
items.implication: Report how approaches handled recommendation wording and handover to primary care.

summary: Five composite voices on worry, emergency-only patients, responsibility, workload and handover.
